street.gap_assumption: December fiscal year, VA FY label = company fiscal year. Framework path = 2026 guide midpoint 18.3% + 300 bps a year: 2027 21.3% vs consensus 21.61% = -30.8 bps; 2028 24.3% vs consensus 24.53% = -23.5 bps. FY2026 consensus 18.40% matches the 18.3% guide. The street models the framework exactly (slightly above it). FY2029 consensus not available.
street.source: Baba data_financials fundamentals consensus (Visible Alpha) cid 1005044; guide from document_id 110705; data_compute

evidence_of_progress.note: Adjusted EBITDA margin: Q1 2026 17.71% vs 12.34% (+537.6 bps, VA actuals); Q2 2026 14.9% on $19.4M, 'an expansion of approximately 430 basis points year-over-year' (CFO, doc 110705). 2026 guide about 500 bps of expansion to 18.3%. Delivery is on plan; the issue is growth (revenue consensus FY2027 down 9.7% over 12 months), not margin.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: the new CFO's 300 bps a year framework implies about 21.3% in 2027 and 24.3% in 2028, and consensus sits at 21.61% and 24.53%. The 4-month EBITDA revision is flat (-0.01%), so the street has underwritten it; the 12-month cut (-12.0% EBITDA, -9.7% revenue) is a growth issue.
verdict: Cheap versus its own history with a new external CFO and a dated numeric framework, but the street already models the 300 bps a year exactly, so there is no margin gap to underwrite; the debate is growth.
open_questions: Why did FY2027 revenue consensus fall 9.7% in 12 months while the margin path held: bank win rates, DSSP implementation timing, or termination fee roll-off?
Does Rule of 45 by 2030 need faster growth than the street's 2027 to 2028 revenue path, and will management give a dated EBITDA margin level?
What prompted the two-seat board expansion in March 2026 (Fox, Linville): shareholder pressure or planned refresh?
